original_question: For every graph G whose adjacency matrix is nonsingular, with maximum degree Delta and minimum degree delta, must the graph energy satisfy E(G) >= Delta + delta, with equality only for complete graphs?
target_in_paper: Section 17, Conjecture 21 (Akbari-Hosseinzadeh): a lower bound on the adjacency energy of non-singular graphs in terms of maximum and minimum degree.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target almost verbatim: it is about the adjacency energy E(G), assumes the adjacency matrix is non-singular, uses the maximum and minimum degrees Δ and δ, asks for the inequality E(G) ≥ Δ + δ, and includes the paper’s equality claim that equality should occur only for complete graphs.
missing_details: The paper works throughout with simple, undirected, unweighted graphs; your draft leaves this ambient graph class implicit.
E(G) should be defined explicitly as the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix A(G).
Δ and δ should be written as Δ(G) and δ(G), the maximum and minimum vertex degrees of G.
The phrase "adjacency matrix is nonsingular" should be made explicit as det(A(G)) ≠ 0.
The paper does not impose connectivity or any lower bound on the order of G here; the quantifier is over all such graphs in the stated graph class.
To be fully stand-alone, the equality case should say "if and only if G is a complete graph" (equivalently, G ≅ K_n), rather than just "complete graphs."
As a research question faithful to the paper, it should be phrased as a conjectural question ("Is it true that...?") rather than as an already established fact.
refined_question: Is the following Akbari–Hosseinzadeh conjecture true? For every simple undirected unweighted graph G with non-singular adjacency matrix A(G) (that is, det(A(G)) ≠ 0), if E(G) = Σ_i |λ_i(G)| denotes the adjacency energy of G and Δ(G), δ(G) denote the maximum and minimum degrees of G, then E(G) ≥ Δ(G) + δ(G), with equality if and only if G is a complete graph.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s Section 17, Conjecture 21, whose wording matches your inequality and equality case essentially exactly. The nearby context needed to make the question self-contained is split across the introduction, where the paper fixes the graph model and notation A(G), Δ(G), δ(G), and the start of Section 17, where it defines graph energy E(G). The immediate discussion after Conjecture 21 also explains why the non-singularity hypothesis is paper-critical: if one drops it, complete bipartite graphs K_{Δ,δ} with Δ > δ give counterexamples since they have zero eigenvalues and energy 2√(Δδ) < Δ + δ. So the refined question should stay exactly at Conjecture 21, not broaden to singular graphs or to a stronger energy bound.
